key_insight: Continual learning for deepfake detectors can worsen demographic unfairness over time, and accuracy recovery does not reliably translate into fairer outcomes.
engineering_relevance: For deployed detection systems, model-update strategies must be evaluated not only for forgetting and accuracy, but also for fairness across evolving user and content demographics.
method: Analyzed four fairness dimensions across diverse demographics.
Trained detectors progressively on 11 real-world deepfake generation methods in chronological order.
Compared CL families including rehearsal, prompts, and regularization.
evidence_signal: The study tracks fairness metrics over time on a chronological sequence of 11 deepfake generators, exposing method- and intersection-dependent shifts in fairness and accuracy.
watch_item: Fairness gains are scarce and inequitable forgetting may stem from representation learning, so mitigation strategies should not rely on class balance or replay alone.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
